title: Map: progressive reveal workflow — file-edit + redeploy
description:
## Background
The GM needs to reveal map features to players incrementally as sessions progress — not all secrets at once. The mechanism is `world/data/player-revealed.json` (created in HeroHeaven-ahg). This issue documents and validates the end-to-end GM workflow.

## Blocked by
HeroHeaven-ahg (schema), HeroHeaven-aqo (GM styling)

## The three-state model
| Feature state | GM build | Public player build |
|---|---|---|
| `visibility: public` | full render | full render |
| `visibility: gm_secrets` | dim render (GM-only) | hidden |
| ID in `player-revealed.json` | full render | full render |

## GM workflow (file-edit)
1. During/after session: identify feature(s) players discovered
2. Open `world/data/player-revealed.json`
3. Add the feature's GeoJSON ID to `revealed[]` array (e.g. `"location_jade-gate"`)
4. Commit + push → Netlify rebuilds public map → players see the new marker

Feature IDs follow the pattern:
- Locations: `location_<slug>` (e.g. `location_jade-gate`)
- Regions: `region_<id>` (e.g. `region_tarim_basin`)
- Routes: `route_<id>`

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] Verify generator correctly promotes revealed IDs in both public and GM builds
- [ ] Write a reference comment block at the top of `player-revealed.json` with ID format and examples
- [ ] Audit all `gm_secrets` features in GeoJSON and list their IDs in a comment section in the JSON (so GM has a quick lookup during play without opening the GeoJSON)
- [ ] Test full cycle: add ID → generate → confirm feature appears in public output
- [ ] Document workflow in `lat.md/locations.md` under a 'GM Reveal Workflow' heading
- [ ] Note upgrade path: future issue for in-map UI that generates updated JSON for download

## Future upgrade hook
The file-edit workflow works. When it becomes friction, replace step 2–4 with a GM-build UI: click feature → 'Reveal to players' → downloads updated `player-revealed.json` → GM replaces file + commits.

## Files
- `world/data/player-revealed.json` (created in HeroHeaven-ahg)
- `utilities/locations/generate_locations_html.py`
- `lat.md/locations.md`

## Notes

title: Map: GM-build styling — distinct render for gm_secrets features
description:
## Background
Once the visibility schema (HeroHeaven-ahg) is in place, the GM build includes `gm_secrets` features. But right now they'd render identically to public features — the GM has no visual cue about what players can vs can't see.

## Goal
In the GM build, `gm_secrets` features render with a distinct visual treatment so the GM can clearly distinguish secret vs revealed at a glance.

## Blocked by
HeroHeaven-ahg (unified visibility schema must be in place first)

## Design
- `gm_secrets` features: lower icon opacity (e.g. 0.45), gold dashed ring or tint
- Features in `player-revealed.json`: render at full normal opacity (identical to public features) — GM sees them as players will
- `public` features: normal render

  - Optional: add a faint dashed circle overlay to distinguish from public markers
- [ ] Revealed features (IDs in player-revealed.json): include in the standard public-style layer, not the gm layer

title: Map: unified visibility schema — gm_secrets vocabulary + reveal manifest
description:
## Background
The map has ad-hoc visibility handling: one feature uses `visibility: 'secret'` (Jade Gate in the GeoJSON), the generator has a --public flag that strips it, and location markdown uses a separate `visibility: public | gm_secrets` frontmatter system. These need to converge on one vocabulary.

This is the foundational issue — HeroHeaven-aqo (GM styling) and HeroHeaven-k9u (progressive reveal workflow) are blocked on this.

## Design philosophy: deny by default
ALL map features are `gm_secrets` unless explicitly promoted. The public player map starts empty — no markers at all — and locations are unlocked one by one via `player-revealed.json` as players discover them. There is no implicit 'public' default.

Three-state model:
| State | GM build | Public build |
|---|---|---|
| `visibility: gm_secrets` (default) | dim render | hidden |
| `visibility: public` | full render | shown |
| ID in `player-revealed.json` | full render | shown |

Note: `visibility: public` is reserved for features the GM decides are always player-visible regardless of discovery (e.g. a location on the campaign frame). Most features should stay `gm_secrets` and flow through the reveal manifest.

## Implementation checklist

### GeoJSON standardization
- [ ] In `world/data/tarim-shaiel-locations.geojson`: add `"visibility": "gm_secrets"` to ALL features (including those currently missing the field)
- [ ] Fix the one existing outlier: `visibility: 'secret'` on Jade Gate → `'gm_secrets'`
- [ ] Same audit for `tarim-shaiel-regions.geojson` and `tarim-shaiel-routes.geojson`

### Generator
- [ ] Update public-build filter: include feature only if `visibility == 'public'` OR feature ID is in `player-revealed.json`
- [ ] Strip `'secret'` and `'gm_secrets'` features from public build (currently only strips `'secret'`)
- [ ] GM build (no --public flag): include all features

### Reveal manifest
- [ ] Create `world/data/player-revealed.json`:
  ```json
  {
    "_comment": "Feature IDs promoted to player-visible. Edit + commit + push to deploy.",
    "_id_format": "location_<slug> | region_<id> | route_<id>",
    "revealed": []
  }
  ```
- [ ] Generator reads this file; any feature ID in `revealed[]` is included in the public build regardless of its `visibility` value

### Documentation
- [ ] Update `lat.md/locations.md` with the deny-by-default model and three-state table
- [ ] Note: public player map intentionally starts blank; that is correct behaviour

## Files
- `world/data/tarim-shaiel-locations.geojson`
- `world/data/tarim-shaiel-regions.geojson`
- `world/data/tarim-shaiel-routes.geojson`
- `world/data/player-revealed.json` (new)
- `utilities/locations/generate_locations_html.py`
- `lat.md/locations.md`

title: Map: zoom choreography — tiered minzoom/maxzoom by feature category
description:
## Background
The world map currently renders all location types at the same zoom threshold (minzoom:4). Regions never disappear when zooming in. This flattens the discovery experience — cities, waystations, and sub-locations all pop on simultaneously.

## Goal
Introduce zoom tiers so the map reveals detail progressively as the player zooms in, and regions fade out as city-level detail takes over.

## Zoom tier targets (draft — adjust after playtesting)
| Tier | Categories | minzoom | maxzoom |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regions | region polygons | 2 | 7 |
| Routes | all routes | 3 | — |
| Major | city, sacred-site | 5 | — |
| Minor | route-node, caravanserai, oasis, landmark | 6 | — |
| Detail | ruins, poi, chokepoint, mountain-pass, power-site, site | 7 | — |

## Implementation checklist
- [ ] In `generate_locations_html.py`: add `maxzoom:7` to regions-fill and regions-line layers
- [ ] Split single `locations` addLayer call into 2–3 calls filtered by category group (MapLibre doesn't support per-feature minzoom on one layer)
  - `locations-major`: filter by category in [city, sacred-site], minzoom:5
  - `locations-minor`: filter by category in [route-node, caravanserai, oasis, landmark, poi], minzoom:6
  - `locations-detail`: remaining categories, minzoom:7
- [ ] Ensure click handler and cursor events apply to all three layers
- [ ] Smoke-test in browser at zoom 3, 5, 6, 7, 8
- [ ] Adjust thresholds based on feel

## Files
- `utilities/locations/generate_locations_html.py` — layer generation (lines ~124–209)
- `docs/world.html` — regenerated output (do not hand-edit)

description:

Owner: Mo · Type: task
Created: 2026-05-07 · Updated: 2026-05-07

DESCRIPTION
## Background

Commit 819d2b3 (2026-05-06) added 4 optional archetype descriptions to PLAYER_PITCH_AND_PRINCIPLES.md and locked Decision 10 (Surrendered-Layer Framework). Audit found three problems introduced by that session.

**Problem 1 — Doubt drift (6 archetypes affected)**
Player-pitch doubts drifted from the method-specific design in PLAYER_ARC_SYNTHESIS. They read as generic character psychology rather than doubts tied to the liberation's unintended consequences (the campaign's core hook).

Specific fixes needed:
- Trickster: restore identity-loss core ('where do the masks go when you take them off?'), not skill-vs-luck
- Crafter: restore consequences-of-creation ('are their things still doing what they were made for?'), not motivation/self-proof
- Healer: restore complacency-enabling ('mending too well makes it easier to ignore what broke it'), NOT the current reversed framing (which puts burden on recipient, not healer)
- Seeker: restore manipulation angle ('whether the questions are theirs'), not knowing-vs-doing
- Sacrificer: restore exploitation angle ('whether choosing to give is ever fully a choice'), not depletion
- Visionary: restore corrupted-sight ('whether what they see is what's there'), not conviction-vs-certainty
- Sentinel: sharpen guardian doubt ('whether they are the barrier or the reason the threat keeps returning to the same door')

**Problem 2 — Keeper is absent**
PLAYER_ARC_SYNTHESIS ranks Keeper #2 in expansion priority (strongest Breaker foil, rich Silk Road material, scene-generating power). The four added in 819d2b3 were Sentinel/Trickster/Crafter/Healer. Keeper was skipped.

Keeper details (from PLAYER_ARC_SYNTHESIS):
- Method: preserves institutions, knowledge, sacred sites — not through fighting but through maintaining
- Gift: knows what's worth keeping when everything is burning
- Doubt: whether what they preserved was worth preserving, or whether holding on was protection dressed as fear
- Tool: key/seal (per PLAYER_ARC_SYNTHESIS; not yet in Decision 10 table)
- Surrendered layer: Custodial — the belief that preservation is inherently virtue
- Foil pair: Breaker ↔ Keeper is the strongest foil in the full roster

**Problem 3 — PLAYER_ARC_SYNTHESIS out of sync**
Still marks four new archetypes as [PROPOSED]; still describes Sentinel as witness/record-keeper (Decision 10 resolved it as guardian/threshold); Keeper is absent from the development status table.

## Implementation Checklist

## Open Questions

value: ARCHETYPE SELF-DOUBT MAP (for narrative consistency): Breaker — Did breaking systems inadvertently free something else? Am I fundamentally destructive? | Warrior — Did overwhelming force scatter rather than destroy? Is strength my blindness? | Seeker — Did knowledge become a weapon? Did I feed the Wizard information? | Visionary — Can I trust my own sight? Was someone else guiding what I could see? | Bridge — Did pragmatism strengthen oppressive systems I was negotiating with? | Sacrificer — Did idealism justify cruelty? | Trickster — Did I outlast every role except the one I can't locate — the original? Who am I when no one needs me to be someone else? | Crafter — Did I serve the need, or did I serve the work?
